رأى طالب برقًا ثم سمع الرعد بعد 3 ثوانٍ. سرعة الصوت نحو 340 م/ث. ما بعد البرق تقريبًا؟

lessons.title: Present perfect
lessons.outcome: Uses the present perfect for experiences and recent results

acts.q: Choose the correct sentence.
opts: I have visited Port Sudan twice.
I have visited Port Sudan yesterday.
I visited Port Sudan twice already have.
I has visited Port Sudan twice.
acts.ex: 'Yesterday' needs the past simple; 'have visited' is correct with 'twice'.

acts.q: Match the verb to its past participle.
Complete: She ___ her homework, so she can play now.
acts.hint: Result in the present; third person singular
acts.ex: Present perfect with 'she' uses 'has'.

acts.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
acts.ex: The past participle of 'go' is 'gone', not 'went'.

lessons.title: Comparatives and superlatives
lessons.outcome: Compares two or more things correctly

acts.q: The Nile is ___ than the Atbara River.
acts.ex: 'long' becomes 'longer' before 'than'.

acts.q: Khartoum is one of ___ cities in Sudan.
acts.ex: 'the largest' compares one city with all others.

acts.q: Match the adjective to its comparative form.
Ali is 150 cm. Hana is 160 cm. Sara is 155 cm. Who is the tallest?
acts.ex: 160 cm is the greatest height.

lessons.title: Modal verbs: can, must, should
lessons.outcome: Chooses modal verbs for ability, obligation and advice

acts.q: You ___ wear a helmet when riding a bike. It is a safety rule.
acts.ex: 'must' expresses a strong obligation.

acts.q: You have a sore throat. A friend says: 'You ___ drink warm water.'
acts.ex: 'should' gives advice.

acts.q: Sort the sentences by meaning.
Which sentence is correct?
opts: He can't to lift the box.
acts.hint: A modal verb is followed by the base verb
acts.ex: After 'can' we use the base form: lift.

lessons.title: Quantifiers: much, many, some, any
lessons.outcome: Uses quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns

acts.q: Sort the nouns.
There aren't ___ chairs in the room.
acts.ex: 'any' is used in negative sentences.

acts.q: Would you like ___ tea?
acts.ex: In offers we usually say 'some'.

acts.q: How ___ milk is there in the bottle?
acts.ex: 'How much' is used with uncountable nouns.

lessons.title: Adverbs of frequency
lessons.outcome: Places adverbs of frequency correctly and reads a routine

acts.q: Put the words in order.
Match the adverb to the meaning.
Read: 'Nada walks to school on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, but takes the bus on Wednesday and Thursday.' How often does she walk?
acts.ex: She walks on most days.

acts.q: Choose the correct sentence.
acts.ex: The adverb goes after 'is'.

lessons.title: Prepositions of place and movement
lessons.outcome: Describes location and movement with prepositions

acts.q: The school is ___ the mosque and the market.
acts.ex: 'between' is used for two things.

acts.q: The boy walked ___ the bridge to cross the river.
acts.hint: From one side to the other
acts.ex: 'across' means from one side to the other.

acts.q: Match the preposition with its meaning.
pairs: from one end to the other inside

acts.q: The library is on the left of the bank. The shop is on the right of the bank. Where is the bank?
opts: between the library and the shop
acts.ex: The bank has the library on its left and the shop on its right.

lessons.title: Prefixes and suffixes

acts.q: Match the word with its opposite.

acts.ex: teacher is the person who teaches.

acts.q: 'Careless' means
acts.ex: The suffix -less means without.

acts.q: Which word is formed correctly?
acts.ex: The opposite of 'kind' is 'unkind'.

lessons.title: Reading for main idea
lessons.outcome: Finds the main idea and supporting details in a short text

acts.q: Read: 'Gum arabic comes from acacia trees. Sudan produces a large share of the world's supply. It is used in food, medicine and drinks.' What is the main idea?
opts: Gum arabic is an important product from Sudan.
acts.hint: What is the whole text about?
acts.ex: All sentences are about gum arabic.

acts.q: According to the text, gum arabic is used in food.
acts.ex: The text says it is used in food, medicine and drinks.

acts.q: What can you infer from the text?
opts: Gum arabic is only used in Sudan.
Gum arabic is useful in many industries.
acts.ex: Because it is used in food, medicine and drinks.

acts.q: Put the sentences in order to make a paragraph.
items: First, farmers cut the bark of the acacia tree.
After a few weeks it becomes hard gum.
Finally, workers collect and sell the gum.

lessons.title: Giving directions
lessons.outcome: Gives and follows directions

acts.q: Put the directions in order.
items: The post office is on your right.

acts.q: 'Take the second turning on the right' means
opts: turn right at the first road
turn right at the second road
acts.ex: 'Second turning' means the second road.

acts.q: Match the phrase with its meaning.

opts: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the hospital?
acts.ex: A polite request uses 'excuse me' and 'could you'.

lessons.title: Writing an informal email

acts.ex: It is formal and polite, not friendly.

acts.q: Which closing is best for an informal email?
acts.ex: 'Take care' is a friendly closing.

lessons.title: Polite requests and offers

opts: Could you open the window, please?
acts.ex: 'Could you...please' is polite.

acts.q: Someone says: 'Would you like some water?' A polite reply is:

acts.q: Match the sentence with its function.

acts.ex: 'Shall I...?' makes an offer.
